title: trust.json acknowledgements sub-document
description: Bulk acknowledgements referenced from trust.json acknowledgements_url, for organizations (e.g. ad networks and SSPs) that accept thousands of grants. Kept off the signature-verification fetch path. Every entry follows the trust.json acknowledgement rules: agent_url MUST be an agents[] entry in the referencing trust.json, and terms come only from the grantor's document. Removing an entry withdraws the acknowledgement; verifiers SHOULD apply the grant source's retention rules (for adcp:adagents, the revoked-publisher-domain retention) before treating a removal as permanent. Normative-sounding language (MUST, SHOULD) in these descriptions records the intended design for a later release and is not enforced by anything in 3.3. Third parties, crawlers and registries MUST NOT treat a published trust.json as authority in 3.3. The v1 in the path is a namespace, not a stability promise: while x-status is experimental the schema may change in breaking ways. EXPERIMENTAL (x-status: experimental, feature id identity.trust_json): schemas only. Nothing in AdCP 3.3 reads, requires, or verifies this document, and brand.json behavior is unchanged. The document name and its /.well-known path may change before graduation (the JournalList trust.txt naming outreach is still open), so do not treat the file name as frozen. See RFC #7809.

next.description: Optional same-host URL of the next shard (untrusted input; see trust.json https_url). Verifiers follow shards in order and stop at a configured limit.
